findings.issue: The cap list for the expansive mode omits the rule that makes the derived cap compatible with the seed range the next paragraph states. `maxFrontierNodes` derives from `maxIterations` as `Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxIterations / 2))` (frontier-admit.cjs:236-240), so the shipped 10-iteration research config caps the frontier at 5, while line 413 says the seed writes 3 to 6 depth-1 nodes. checkProposal skips the run-wide cap entirely while seeding — `if (!seeding && countLiveNodes(nodes) >= caps.maxFrontierNodes) return 'fanout'` (frontier-admit.cjs:352-353) — so a depth-1 seed answers only to the root-children cap (6 for research), and every non-pruned seed, answered ones included, still counts toward the live total that later admissions are checked against. The convergence reference states this in full (convergence.md:68); this section, which enumerates the caps, does not, so a reader who applies the stated cap to the seed predicts a pruned sixth node on a default run.
